metaNotes is free text from the user describing what team traits are currently favored for that op and why — this is meta commentary, not a hard game rule, and can shift over time.

ops.name: Turning Up The Heat
ops.metaNotes: Favors Ranged heroes — the quick wave cadence rewards heroes who don't need to move/reposition, letting them reset and re-engage faster between waves than Melee heroes would.

reportedBenchmarks.note: Reported as "around 85". 600s / 85 waves implies ~7.06 seconds per wave.

ops.name: Train and Gain
ops.metaNotes: Current meta stacks 3-4 copies of Aquarus behind Space Racer as a shield wall for unattended idle clears. The two artifact picks are not generic stat sticks: the Guardians of the Globe Bracelet grants Tech Jacket the 'Original GOTG' tag she does not otherwise have, which single-handedly activates Aquarus's own dormant 'Atlantean Aid' passive (which needs an Original GOTG ally to do anything) and also feeds Body Enhancement's crit-chance-per-GOTG-ally scaling on Space Racer. One artifact placement is quietly switching on two other heroes' passives at once.

currentMeta.duplicateHeroesNote: Asks for 3-4 real, independently-leveled copies of Aquarus (a Rare hero, but still real investment x4) — the single most duplication-heavy lineup the user reported.

artifactAssignments.why: Passive grants crit chance per Original GOTG / GOTG ally on the team — scales with the tag the bracelet below grants to Tech Jacket.

Grants the wielder the 'Original GOTG' tag regardless of their real tags. Tech Jacket does not carry it natively; this is what turns on Aquarus's own 'Atlantean Aid' passive and Space Racer's Body Enhancement crit scaling.

f2pAlternative.rationale: Keep exactly one real Aquarus and the GOTG-tag trick (bracelet stays on Tech Jacket). Replace the other 3 Aquarus slots with two different heroes already worth leveling for other reasons: Atom Eve's 'Strength Through Shielding' passively amplifies ANY shield on the team (including Aquarus's own 'Bubble Boy' cast) +5% value and heals the recipient 5% of her own max HP for free, and Seance Dog's 'Spectral Safeguard' automatically grants bonus shields to its healing because Space Racer already carries the 'Not of this Earth' tag it looks for. Net result: three different defensive triggers instead of four copies of the identical one, for the cost of leveling one Aquarus instead of four.

reportedBenchmarks.note: Reported as "1400+", so this is a LOWER BOUND, not a measurement. 7200s / 1400 waves implies at most ~5.14 seconds per wave — noticeably faster per wave than Turning Up The Heat, which is why cadence is modelled per-op rather than globally.

ops.name: Downtown Destruction
ops.metaNotes: Core of Space Racer / Anissa / Invincible Blue plus 2 flex slots, reported as Tech Jacket, Seance Dog, a 2nd (lower-invested) Invincible Blue, or Rus Livingston. Only one of those four flex options is actually a duplication problem: the 2nd Invincible Blue is real investment in an Elite hero. The other three (Tech Jacket, Seance Dog, Rus Livingston) are all single-copy picks already, so the reported meta already contains an F2P-friendly path — just fill both flex slots from {Tech Jacket, Seance Dog, Rus Livingston} instead of reaching for a 2nd Invincible Blue. Rus Livingston fits the op's own name well: his 'Space Scavenger' heals the team 2% max HP per enemy kill, and a 'Downtown Destruction' clear should have a high enemy-kill count to feed that.

currentMeta.duplicateHeroesNote: Only the "2nd Invincible Blue" flex option is a real duplication cost; the other three reported flex options (Tech Jacket, Seance Dog, Rus Livingston) are single-copy and already F2P-friendly.

f2pAlternative.rationale: Invincible Blue's 'Killer's Instinct' buffs ALL melee allies (life leech + attack) every time he lands a kill — it does not require a second copy of him to benefit from, any melee ally already gets the stacks. Agent Spider fills the second melee slot instead of a duplicate: he is cheaper to invest in, and his own 'Sticking Together' (+5% team crit chance with a Last Line of Defense ally present) is already satisfied by Invincible Blue, who carries that tag. Rus Livingston (confirmed, not Red Rush) is a fine alternative sustain pick straight from the reported flex list — his enemy-kill heal fits a wave-clear op like this one directly.

ops.reportedSynergy: Thula + Anissa + Rus Livingston plus 2 sacrificial Viltrumites works because the sacrificial Viltrumites dying potentiates the trio: Anissa and Thula are the bleed/wound characters, and Rus Livingston heals the whole team after every enemy death. The Viltrumite deaths feed Thula's 'A Lust for Death' (+50% attack per Viltrumite death, ally or enemy) and Lucan's 'Purge Survivor' if he is one of them, while Rus's 'Space Scavenger' converts the resulting kills into sustain.

ops.name: This is Heavy
ops.metaNotes: Two level-1 Multi-Paul copies used purely as disposable bodies — this is a CHEAP duplication (deliberately zero-invested) and not the kind of resource conflict this file is otherwise tracking; Multi-Paul's own kit already self-clones 3 more copies per cast on top of that, so this is already an efficient design. Hidden value-add: General Kregg's 'Tactical Reassignment' charges your highest-attack real ally's main skill 30% and redirects their aggro every time ANY ally is defeated — including the disposable Multi-Pauls — and Cecil Stedman's 'Always Have Backup' separately spawns a bonus Reaniman off that same ally-death trigger. Between the two flex options given (Tech Jacket or Cecil), Cecil is the mechanically stronger pick here specifically because his passive keys off the Multi-Pauls dying; Tech Jacket's kit has no such interaction with ally deaths.

currentMeta.duplicateHeroesNote: Two Multi-Paul copies, but kept at level 1 deliberately — effectively free, not a resource conflict.

ops.name: Well Done
ops.metaNotes: No duplication problem here at all — Cecil Stedman, Omni-Man, Agent Spider, and Rex Splode are 4 distinct real heroes, and they are the same core as the 'Crit Feedback Loop' squad discussed with the user on 2026-07-23 (Rex Splode's 'Cherry Bomb on Top' procs off anyone's crit, Agent Spider's 'Arach-No-More' procs off anyone's stun, Omni-Man self-snowballs off his own crits). If a player is already investing in that crit-loop core for another op, this op is close to free to also clear well.

ops.name: Everyone Who's Anyone
ops.metaNotes: Only one hero named — Invincible, explicitly requiring heavy individual investment — with the rest of the lineup left open. This is already about as F2P-friendly as a single-carry op can be: there is nothing to de-duplicate, only one investment target. Invincible's own 'Going Steady' passive reduces team cooldowns 5% while fighting alongside a Last Line of Defense ally (Agent Spider, Tech Jacket, Invincible Blue, Atom Eve (Armored), Robot Lifepod, and Kid Omni-Man all carry that tag), so one of those is a low-cost pick worth prioritizing over a generic filler for the open slots; the rest can reuse sustain/tank picks already being leveled for other ops (e.g. Allen The Alien, Seance Dog) rather than investing in anything new just for this op. Enemy roster reported as very broad, spanning every faction — no fixed counter-tech to lean on here, unlike the other ops.

flexOptions: unspecified by the user — 4 open slots

ops.name: The Guardians of the Globe
ops.metaNotes: No duplication problem — 5 distinct real heroes across 3 fixed core slots + 2 single-pick flex slots. Both flex choices have a clear tag-driven answer once cross-referenced against the other 3 kits: Doc Seismic (not Kursk) carries both 'Subsoil' and 'Technologist' tags, which respectively feed Volcanikka's 'Under Realm Fury' (gains a DoT-boosting charge when a Subsoil ally is defeated) and Powerplex's 'Technologically Advanced' (+15% energy attack / +6% CDR to any Technologist ally) — Kursk triggers neither. Separately, Universa (not Donald Ferguson) carries 'Not of this Earth', the exact tag Shapesmith's 'Aliens Alliance' passive checks for (+6% team healing, +5% defense) — without a Not of this Earth ally present, that passive sits completely dormant, and Universa is the only flex option that supplies it.

ops.name: Reanimen Rampage
ops.primaryReward: Gold + Hero XP + Hero Special XP (all at a reduced rate vs. their dedicated ops)
ops.metaNotes: An 8th op the user hadn't initially mentioned. Reported meta is one real, well-invested Cecil Stedman plus 4 Level-1 throwaway heroes. The heroes are deliberately kept at Level 1 so they die reliably against even these weak Common enemies, which is the point: Cecil's 4th skill, "Always Have Backup," summons a Reaniman ally (30% of the dying ally's stats) every time a non-summoned ally dies. The 4 Level-1 sacrifices function as a renewable fuel supply for that loop rather than as real combatants — each one dying spawns a fresh ally-Reaniman to keep fighting the enemy Reanimen, letting the 30-minute clock run on largely autonomous combat while Cecil (the only real investment) racks up kill credit and levels quickly. Enemies are exclusively the two Common Reaniman variants — single-target basic attacks only, no AoE/CC — so raw threat is low and the design problem is sustaining a long fight cheaply, not surviving a hard hit.

flexOptions: Multi-Paul (Level 1) x4 or any 4 cheap Level-1 heroes as sacrifice fodder
currentMeta.duplicateHeroesNote: The 4 sacrifices are interchangeable Level-1 throwaways by design — cheap on purpose, not a resource conflict.

f2pAlternative.rationale: Speculative alternative to test, not a confirmed equal: since the enemies are exclusively weak, single-target Common Reanimen with no AoE or crowd control, a hard-AoE-clear squad may out-farm the attrition-loop approach on raw kill volume within the fixed 30-minute window instead of relying on Cecil's summon-on-death trick. Rus Livingston's "Swarm of Sequids" AoE stun plus his enemy-kill team heal, Rex Splode's AoE bomb (which also procs off any ally's crit), and Multi-Paul's self-cloning triple-attack all shred a weak single-target-only enemy roster fast. Caveat: this hasn't been confirmed to match Cecil's specific advantage of concentrating kill credit onto one investment target — that depends on how this game attributes per-kill XP, which is not something this data set can verify. Worth A/B testing in-game before committing resources.
